rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet called the prayer command in this verse the most hopeful verse in the Book.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول " أرجى آية في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river: prayer removes sins as washing removes bodily dirt.
rows.anchor: إن أحدكم ليقوم من وضوئه فتساقط عن جوارحه الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that persistence in good deeds leads a person to abandon evil deeds, as though the good deeds remove them.
rows.anchor: الدوام على فعل الحسنات يدعو إلى ترك السيئات فكأنها يذهبن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation identifies the good deeds as repentance, which removes sins by cancelling their punishment; the author says there is no disagreement that repentance cancels punishment.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحسنات التوبة فإنها تذهب السيئات بأن تسقط عقابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is an admonition for whoever reflects on the teaching that good deeds remove evil deeds.
rows.anchor: فيه تذكار وموعظة لمن تذكر به وفكر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here patience may mean steadfastness in prayer, as in the command to order one's family to pray and persist in it.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه واصبر على الصلاة كما قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the reward of the doers of good here as referring to those who pray.
rows.anchor: أي المصلين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command tells Muhammad to endure his people's harm and denial, fulfil obligations, and avoid blameworthy acts; God fully rewards good-doers.
rows.anchor: اصبر يا محمد على أذى قومك وتكذيبهم إياك وعلى القيام بما افترضته عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means that earlier peoples had no people of discernment who forbade corruption, despite God's gifts of reason, messengers, and proofs.
rows.anchor: كان يجب أن يكون منهم قوم بهذه الصفة مع إنعام الله تعالى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes those who followed the corrupt paths of peoples such as ʿĀd and Thamūd, and marvels that they agreed in unbelief until punishment destroyed them.
rows.anchor: كيف اجتمعوا على الكفر حتى استأصلهم الله بالعذاب وأنواع العقوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'people of discernment' is also explained as people of religion and goodness, or blessing, or discernment and obedience.
rows.anchor: قيل: أولوا بقية عناه ذوو دين وخير. وقيل: معناه ذوو بركة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The few saved people who forbade corruption were the prophets and righteous believers; the exception is grammatically disconnected because the preceding construction is affirmative, not a formal negation.
rows.anchor: قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد وهم الأنبياء والصالحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned people pursued accustomed luxury and pleasures instead of the affairs of the afterlife, persisting in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ما عودوا من النعم والتنعم وإيثار اللذات على أمور الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the duty to forbid wrong: God censures those who neglected it and says He saved the few who did it; had the many forbidden it, they would not have perished.
rows.anchor: في الآية دلالة على وجوب النهي عن المنكر لأنه سبحانه ذمهم بترك النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God does not destroy towns by injustice on His part; He destroys them only for their own injustice. The excerpt ends before the remaining interpretations.
rows.anchor: منه لهم ولكن إنما يهلكهم بظلمهم لأنفسهم كما قال:

rows.speaker: علي، علي بن الحسين، محمد بن علي، جعفر بن محمد، الحسن، يحيى بن يعمر، قتادة، مجاهد، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: These readers are reported, with some disagreement, to read شعفها with ʿayn; the remaining readers use شغفها with ghayn.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد بخلاف وابن محيصن قد شعفها بالعين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar is reported to read متكا without hamza and with a doubled tā; the other readers use متكأ with hamza and doubling.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي جعفر متكا بغير همز مشدد التاء والباقون متكأ بالهمزة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading from Mujahid has متكا with a light, vowelless tā; Ibn Abbas is also reported to read it this way.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة مجاهد متكا خفيفة ساكنة التاء وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads حاشى لله with an alif; the remaining readers read حاش لله without it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمر وحاشى لله والباقون حاش لله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبي كعب، الحسن
rows.claim: Noncanonical variants include حاش الله from Ibn Masʿud and Ubayy, حاش الإله from al-Hasan, and a second al-Hasan form with a vowelless shīn.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود وأبي كعب حاش الله وعن الحسن حاش الإله

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub alone reads السجن with fatḥa on the sīn, treating it as a verbal noun; the others use kasra for the place-name.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وحده السجن أحب إلي بفتح السين والباقون بكسرها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the ʿayn reading as love taking her in every direction, from the word for mountain peaks; the phrase describes love carrying her to its furthest degree.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: معنى شعفها بالعين ذهب بها كل مذهب

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says the love reached her heart and nearly burned it, comparing the word's origin to the heat of treating a camel with tar.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جني: معناه وصل حبه إلى قلبها فكاد يحرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common ghayn reading means that Yusuf's love pierced the heart's covering and reached the heart itself.
rows.anchor: شغفها بالغين فمعناه أنه خرق شغاف قلبها وهو غلافه فوصل إلى قلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متكأ can mean something on which people lean while eating, drinking, or talking; its form is derived from اتكأ.
rows.anchor: وأما المتكأ فهو ما يتكأ عليه الطعام أو شراب أو حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متكا may be derived from tying a waterskin shut, and المتك may mean citron; another view calls it a kind of stew.
rows.anchor: وأما من قرأ متكا فيجوز أن يكون مفتعلا من قوله:

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects taking حاشى لله as a preposition here: it cannot govern a like particle; he treats it as a verb meaning Yusuf kept away from the accusation for fear of God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي لا يخلو قولهم حاشى لله من أن يكون الحرف الجار

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: The poet's phrase حاشى أبي ثوبان is cited as evidence for Abu ʿAmr's form حاشى لله.
rows.anchor: وأما حجة أبي عمرو في قوله حاشى لله فقول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz means powerful and invulnerable; the title suited the minister because kingship and broad authority protected him.
rows.anchor: العزيز المنيع بقدرته يضام في أمره وسمي بذلك لأنه كان ملكا ممتنعا بملكه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم، الزجاج
rows.claim: The Arabs use fatā and fatāt for young people and also call a male slave fatā.
rows.anchor: والفتى الغلام الشاب والمرأة فتاة قال أبو مسلم والزجاج:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makar is plotting by artifice to obtain what one seeks; a makūra leg is tightly formed.
rows.anchor: والمكر الفتل بالحيلة إلى ما يراد من الطلبة وجارية ممكورة الساقين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The cushion is the leaning pillow; citron is another reported meaning, but Abu ʿUbayda rejects inferring citron from this expression alone.
rows.anchor: المتكأ الوسادة وهو النمرق الذي يتكأ عليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda rejects the claim that أكبرنه means the women menstruated on seeing Yusuf, saying the usage is unknown and the cited poem is fabricated.
rows.anchor: والبيت مصنوع لا يعرفه العلماء بالشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say أكبرنه means they menstruated from awe, though the language does not establish that sense.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى أكبرنه أنهن حضن حين رأينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prison is confinement that prevents a person from acting freely; iʿtiṣām is refraining from sin, while istiʿṣām asks God for protection.
rows.anchor: والسجن المنع عن التصرف بالحبس سجن يسجن سجنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāghirūn denotes people in humiliation and disgrace; ṣabā is the heart's tenderness and inclination.
rows.anchor: والصاغرين من الصغار صغر بصغر صغارا وهو الذل والهوان والصبا رقة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem is cited to show ṣabā as tender inclination of the heart.
rows.anchor: إلى هند صبا قلبي وهند مثلها يصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says prison is easier to bear than the sexual sin the women invite him to commit; the plural indicates that the women joined the Aziz's wife in inviting him.
rows.anchor: السجن أحب إلي وأسهل علي مما يدعونني إليه من الفاحشة

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Thumali reports from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn that after leaving the wife, each woman secretly sent to Yusuf asking him to visit her.
rows.anchor: في حديث أبي حمزة الثمالي عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام أن النسوة لما خرجن من عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the women urged Yusuf to obey their mistress, arguing that she was wronged and he was the wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: إنهن قلن له أطع مولاتك واقض حاجتها فإنها المظلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the wife let each woman meet Yusuf alone, and each then invited him to herself.
rows.anchor: فلما خلون به دعته كل واحدة منهن إلى نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf does not mean that he positively desires prison: prison is itself sinful if meant as a chosen act, so the phrase means that it is less difficult and easier to bear.
rows.anchor: لم يرد المحبة التي هي الإرادة وإنما أراد أن ذلك أخف علي وأسهل

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi reads the phrase as preferring to prepare himself to endure prison rather than prepare himself for adultery.
rows.anchor: توطيني النفس على السجن أحب إلي من توطيني النفس على الزنى عن أبي علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asks God to turn away their scheme through divine لطف, since their scheme had already taken place; ṣabā means inclining to them or their words with desire.
rows.anchor: أمل إليهن أو إلى قولهن بهواي والصبوة لطافة الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'among the ignorant' means either deserving blame for ignorance or acting as though ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي المستحقين لصفة الذم بالجهل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Yusuf's prayer and protected him from the women's plot.
rows.anchor: فأجاب له ربه فيما دعاه فعصمه من مكرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A renewed supplication may be the condition for a beneficial divine لطف; without it, that لطف might not occur, so Yusuf can ask despite expecting God's care.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تتعلق المصلحة بالألطاف عند الدعاء المجدد

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi argues that the verse permits supplication for something one knows God will do, since Yusuf knew God would grant لطف if he had it.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: في الآية دلالة على جواز الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage does not prove al-Jubbaʾi's conclusion: Yusuf may have asked because he thought a لطف could be granted only after prayer and absent without it.
rows.anchor: ولا تدل الآية على ما قاله لما قلناه من أنه يجوز أن يكون سأله لتجويزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the supplicant and knows the sincerity of the prayer and whether an answer will benefit or harm the person.
rows.anchor: السميع لدعاء الداعي العليم بإخلاصه في دعائه وبما يصلحه من الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the women were previously mentioned, the masculine plural 'them' refers to the king; another reading takes it as Zuleikha and her helpers, with masculine agreement for a mixed group.
rows.anchor: أراد به زليخا وأعوانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs proving Yusuf's innocence were the shirt torn from behind and the women's cut hands, according to Qatada and others.
rows.anchor: العلامات الدالة على براءة يوسف وهي قد القميص من دبره وجز الأيدي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the signs as evidence that the women had despaired of obtaining Yusuf.
rows.anchor: العلامات الدالة على الإياس منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical subject of بدا is omitted and understood as بداء; the decision that appeared was the decision to imprison him.
rows.anchor: وقوله بدا فاعله مضمر وتقديره ثم بدا لهم بداء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Zuleikha told her husband that Yusuf had publicly disgraced her by saying she had seduced him, and demanded release to explain herself or his imprisonment.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: وذلك إن المرأة قالت لزوجها إن هذا العبد قد فضحني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says they imprisoned Yusuf so the public would assume he was guilty, since criminals are the ones imprisoned.
rows.anchor: الغرض من الحبس أن يظهر للناس أن الذنب كان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the prison was near Zuleikha, who wanted to see Yusuf when she looked out.
rows.anchor: كان الحبس قريبا منها فأرادت أن يكون بقربها حتى إذا أشرفت عليه رأته

rows.speaker: عكرمة، الكلبي، الجبائي
rows.claim: The imprisonment lasted seven years according to ʿIkrima, five according to al-Kalbi, or until the affair was forgotten and Yusuf's news faded according to al-Jubbaʾi.
rows.anchor: إلى سبع سنين عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The citation to call people to God's path with wisdom frames the account of Yusuf's religious address to the prisoners.
rows.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prisoners said they had come to love Yusuf; he replied that affection for him had repeatedly brought him hardship: his aunt's love led to a theft accusation, his father's to the well, and the Aziz's wife's to prison.
rows.anchor: لا تحباني فوالله ما أحبني أحد إلا دخل علي من حبه بلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣāḥib is a close and particular companion; the two companions of prison are Yusuf's fellow inmates.
rows.anchor: وصاحبا السجن هما الملازمان له بالكون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's question contrasts many divided, powerless stone and wooden idols with the one irresistible God, and serves to establish the proof rather than request information.
rows.anchor: وهذا ظاهره الاستفهام والمراد به التقرير وإلزام الحجة والقاهر هو القادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf first addresses two inmates, then uses the plural because he intends everyone in their condition, or everyone in the prison.
rows.anchor: ابتدأ بخطاب اثنين ثم خاطب بلفظ الجمع لأنه قصد جميع من هو في مثل حالهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols' names are empty labels for supposed gods; God has given no proof for worshipping them.
rows.anchor: أسماء فارغة عن المعاني لا حقيقة لها ما أنزل الله من حجة بعبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God has judgment and command, and only He may be worshipped; the religion described is straight and free of deviation.
rows.anchor: ما الحكم والأمر إلا لله فلا يجوز العبادة والخضوع والتذلل إلا لله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people do not know what reward obedience brings and what punishment disobedience brings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما للمطيعين من الثواب وللعاصين من العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they do not know the truth because they have turned away from reasoning and proof.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمون صحة ما أقوله لعدولهم عن النظر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer's three grape clusters meant three more days in prison, then release on the fourth day and restoration to his post; Yusuf calls his master 'lord' as one says lord of a house or estate.
rows.anchor: أما العناقيد الثلاثة فإنها ثلاثة أيام تبقى في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other prisoner's baskets meant three more days before he was crucified and birds ate from his head; Yusuf's certain forecast shows he spoke by revelation of the unseen, not ordinary interpretation.
rows.anchor: أما السلال الثلاث فإنها ثلاثة أيام تبقى في السجن ثم يخرجك الملك فيصلبك

rows.speaker: أكثرون، الجبائي
rows.claim: The majority and al-Jubbaʾi take ظن as certain knowledge received by revelation, as in the verse about expecting to meet one's account; this is the author's preferred reading.
rows.anchor: هذا قول الأكثرين واختيار الجبائي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes ظن in its ordinary sense of conjecture, since Yusuf could not verify that the prisoner's dream report was true.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة للذي ظنه ناجيا لأنه لا يحكم بصدقه فيما قصه من الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asked the escaped cupbearer to mention that he was unjustly imprisoned to his master, the king.
rows.anchor: أي اذكرني عند سيدك بأني محبوس ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author first explains Satan's making Yusuf forget as Yusuf forgetting to mention God and instead asking a human for help, when reliance on God was more fitting.
rows.anchor: يعني أنسى الشيطان يوسف ذكر الله تعالى في تلك الحال حتى استغاث بمخلوق

rows.speaker: الحسن، محمد بن إسحاق، الجبائي، أبو مسلم
rows.claim: An alternative takes the forgotten remembrance as the cupbearer's failure to mention Yusuf to the king; the author paraphrases this as Satan making him forget Yusuf before his master.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ومحمد بن إسحاق والجبائي وأبي مسلم وعلى هذا فتقديره فأنساه الشيطان ذكر يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، علي بن الحسين، أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The stay of several years is specified as seven years in reports from Ibn Abbas, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, and Abu ʿAbd Allah.
rows.anchor: أي سبع سنين عن ابن عباس وروي ذلك عن علي بن الحسين ع وأبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet marvels that Yusuf sought help from a creature instead of the Creator; another says his request to be remembered prolonged his stay.
rows.anchor: عجبت من أخي يوسف ع كيف استغاث بالمخلوق دون الخالق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report from Abu ʿAbd Allah, Gabriel asks Yusuf who gave him his beauty, his father's love, the caravan, rescue from the well, and protection from the women; Yusuf answers that God did, and is told to remain in prison for turning to a creature.
rows.anchor: جاء جبرائيل ع فقال: يا يوسف من جعلك أحسن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking human help to avert harm is permitted and can even be required; the Prophet sought help from the Emigrants and Helpers, so the reports describe a temporary reproach for departing from Yusuf's usual reliance on God, not a prohibition.
rows.anchor: الاستعانة بالعباد في دفع المضار والتخلص من المكاره جائز غير منكر ولا قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson is to rely on and seek help from God in hardship, although seeking help from other people is also permissible.
rows.anchor: ترغيب في الاعتصام بالله تعالى والاستعانة به دون غيره عند نزول الشدائد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says buḍʿ denotes a span from three to five years.
rows.anchor: البضع ما بين الثلاث إلى الخمس عن أبي عبيده

rows.speaker: قطرب، مجاهد
rows.claim: Qutrub defines buḍʿ as three to seven; this definition is also reported from Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وقول قطرب مروي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الأصمعي، قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi gives three to nine, as reported by al-Zajjaj, and this range is transmitted from Qatada.
rows.anchor: وقول الأصمعي مروي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines buḍʿ as less than ten; most commentators specify seven years in this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وهو ما دون العشرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the seven years in prison came after the five years already spent there.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: وهذه السبع سوى الخمسة التي كانت قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allah says Gabriel taught Yusuf a prayer to recite after every obligatory prayer, asking God for relief and provision from expected and unexpected sources.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: علم جبرائيل ع يوسف في حبسه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report through Shuʿayb al-ʿAqraqufi says that when the term ended, Yusuf prayed for release by invoking Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob; Abu ʿAbd Allah tells the questioner to make the same prayer through Muhammad, ʿAli, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, and the Imams.
rows.anchor: وروى شعيب العقرقوفي عنه ع قال: لما انقضت المدة

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads دأبا with fatḥa on the hamza; the other readers use sukūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص دأبا بفتح الهمزة والباقون بسكونها

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: The Kufan readers except ʿAsim use the second-person reading تعصرون; the remaining readers use the third-person يعصرون.
rows.anchor: قرأ تعصرون بالتاء أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن عمر، الضحاك، قتادة، زيد بن علي
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading uses بعد أمه, with هā, and is attributed to these readers, with disagreement in the transmissions from Ibn Abbas and Ibn ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس وابن عمر بخلاف والضحاك وقتادة وزيد بن علي

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli reads بعد أمة with kasra on the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الأشهب العقيلي بعد أمة بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads سبع سنابل rather than the form used in the verse text.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد عليهما السلام وسبع سنابل

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad is also reported to read ما قربتم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيضا ما قربتم

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد، الأعرج، عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: These readers use a form of يعصرون with a damma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ṣād.
rows.anchor: قرأ هو والأعرج وعيسى بن عمر وفيه يعصرون بياء مضمومة وصاد مفتوحة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says دأبا is an accusative verbal noun supported by the sense of تزرعون: you work persistently at planting; its fatḥa may also be a dialectal variant.
rows.anchor: انتصب دأبا بما دل عليه تزرعون وفي علاج ودؤوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يعصرون can mean pressing oil, water, or juice from produce, fitting the return of prosperity after a drought; some say they had pressed neither oil nor wine for fourteen years.
rows.anchor: من العصر الذي يراد به الضغط الذي يلحق ما فيه دهن أو ماء نحو الزيتون

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل، أبو زبيد الطائي، أبو عبيدة، لبيد
rows.claim: Another sense of العصر is seeking refuge or means of rescue; Ibn Muqbil, Abu Zubayd, Abu ʿUbayda, and Labid provide poetic evidence for rescue or escape.
rows.anchor: وهذا يمكن أن يكون تأويل الآية عليه لأن من المتأولين من يحكى أنهم لم يعصروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ form refers to the previously mentioned people; the tāʾ form addresses the people who requested interpretation, and may include others as well.
rows.anchor: فأما من قال: يعصرون بالياء فإنه جعل الفاعلين الناس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAli rejects a reading that would imply people press wine during the famine year and directs the reader to a form meaning they receive rain after famine.
rows.anchor: فقال ويحك وأي شيء يعصرون أيعصرون الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams may come from God or angels and admit interpretation, from Satan without interpretation, or from the sleeper's beliefs and prior thoughts.
rows.anchor: منها ما يكون من الله تعالى وملائكته وهو الذي له تعبير وتأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaf denotes loss of fat; aʿjaf and ʿajfāʾ are the masculine and feminine forms, with ʿijāf as an unusual plural.
rows.anchor: والعجف ذهاب السمن والذكر أعجف والأنثى عجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḍghāth al-aḥlām means confused dreams; a ḍighth is a bundle or handful, and al-Tirmidhi specifies a handful of grass.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي: الضغث ملء اليد من الحشيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition makes a ḍighth a confused mixture of straw, irregular and incoherent like tangled dreams.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضغث خلط قش المد وهو غير متشاكل ولا متلائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iddikār comes from remembrance: its original tāʾ changes to dāl and assimilates with dhāl; the alternative اذكر is possible, though dāl is better.
rows.anchor: وأصله اذتكار لكن التاء أبدل منها الدال وأدغمت الذال في الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umma may mean a group united in purpose or a period of time; ṣiddīq means strongly affirming the truth or especially truthful.
rows.anchor: والأمة الجماعة تؤم أمرا والأمة المدة وهي الجملة من الحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatwā answers a ruling; a reply to a question that is not about a ruling is not technically a fatwā.
rows.anchor: والفتيا الجواب عن حكم المعنى وقد يكون الجواب عن نفس المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʾb means habit or effort; dhar and daʿ lack past-tense forms because taraka serves that function.
rows.anchor: والدأب العادة يقال: دأب يدأب دأبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shidda, solidity, and difficulty are near synonyms; another account lists seven uses of shidda, including time, anger, pain, drink, and the body.
rows.anchor: والشدة والصلابة والصعوبة نظائر. وقيل: الشدة تكون في سبعة أصناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥṣān is protection, like placing something within a guard or enclosure.
rows.anchor: والإحصان مثل الإحراز أحصنه إحصانا جعله في حرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawth is help that meets an urgent need and removes harm; ghayth is rain arriving when it is needed.
rows.anchor: والغوث هو نفع يأتي على شدة حاجة ينفي المضرة ومنه الغيث المطر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The lām in للرؤيا clarifies what is being interpreted; it is normally added to a fronted object, though examples also occur without fronting.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء فيما ليس بمقدم من المفعول نحو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخر is indeclinable because it departs from the usual definite-alif-lām pattern for feminine forms, like وسط and كبر.
rows.anchor: وآخر لا ينصرف لأنه صرف عن جهة صواحبها التي جاءت بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction أضغاث أحلام is understood as 'they are confused dreams,' and the address يوسف omits the vocative particle, as in a cited line addressing Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وفي آخر { أضغاث أحلام } تقديره هي أضغاث أحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was the Egyptian ruler al-Walid ibn Rayyan, and al-ʿAziz was his minister; the majority understand the vision as occurring in sleep.
rows.anchor: ملك مصر وهو الوليد بن ريان والعزيز وزيره وفيما رواه الأكثرون إني أرى في منامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven lean cows consume the fat ones until they disappear; the dry ears curl over and overcome the green ears.
rows.anchor: فدخلت السمان في بطون المهازيل حتى لم أر منهن شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king addresses the elite; another view says the assembly was magicians and soothsayers.
rows.anchor: جمع الأشراف. وقيل: جمع السحرة والكهنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assembly calls the dream confused false dreams that cannot be interpreted; al-Kalbi calls them false dreams and Qatada calls them a jumble.
rows.anchor: أباطيل أحلام عن الكلبي. وقيل: تخاليط أحلام عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: After a long time, the escaped cupbearer remembered Yusuf and what he had instructed him; the account is attributed to these authorities.
rows.anchor: تذكر شأن يوسف وما وصاه به بعد حين من الدهر وزمان طويل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf interprets the seven fat cows and green ears as seven fertile years and the lean cows and dry ears as seven years of famine.
rows.anchor: فالسنون الجدبة وأما البقرات السمان والسنابل السبع الخضر فإنهن سبع سنين مخصبات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes دأبا as consecutive years of planting, following the people's usual practice.
rows.anchor: أي فازرعوا سبع سنين متوالية عن ابن عباس أي زراعة متوالية في هذه السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, دأبا means planting diligently, or functions as an adverb meaning they will keep working at it.
rows.anchor: دأبا أي بجد واجتهاد في الزراعة ويجوز أن يكون حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should leave all but the grain they eat in its ears and not thresh it, because storage in the ear better preserves it from spoilage.
rows.anchor: اتركوه { في سنبله } لا تذروه ولا تدوسوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says insects do not infest grain while it remains in the ear, whereas threshed grain spoils sooner.
rows.anchor: السنبل لا يقع فيه سوس ولا يهلك وإن بقي مدة من الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven severe years will consume the stored harvest saved for them; the years are described as eating because the famine occurs during them.
rows.anchor: تأكلن فيها ما قدمتم في السنين المخصبة لتلك السنين وإنما أضاف الأكل إلى السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating can also mean using up and destroying something, as in the idiom that a journey ate a camel's flesh.
rows.anchor: أراد بالأكل الإفناء والإهلاك كما يقال: أكل السير لحم الناقة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Yusuf prepared food for two; when the guest ate his whole portion one day, Yusuf recognized that the seven severe years had begun.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم كان يوسف يصنع طعام اثنين فيقربه إلى رجل فيأكل نصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should preserve a small amount from the harvest, since تحصنون means storing and protecting it.
rows.anchor: إلا شيئا قليلا مما تحرزون وتدخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final year brings rain and relief; يَغاث may refer either to rainfall or to rescue from drought.
rows.anchor: يمطر الناس من الغيث. وقيل: يغاثون من الغوث والغياث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say people will press fruits such as grapes, olives, and sesame in the prosperous year.
rows.anchor: الثمار التي تعصر في الخصب كالعنب والزيت والسمسم عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يَعصرون may mean they escape famine by resorting to a means of rescue; the verse is illustrated by a poetic image of thirst and reliance on water.
rows.anchor: لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق كنت كالغصان بالماء اعتصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's forecast of the prosperous year goes beyond the king's dream and question, and is knowledge of the unseen God disclosed as a sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول من يوسف إخبار بما لم يسألوه منه ولم يكن في رؤيا الملك

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi says the episode disproves that dreams become true according to their first interpretation: the assembly called the king's dream confused, yet Yusuf correctly interpreted it.
rows.anchor: قال البلخي: وهذا التأويل من يوسف يدل على بطلان قول من يقول

rows.speaker: الأعشى، البرجمي
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha and al-Barjami, transmitting from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, read النسوة with a ḍamma on the nūn; the rest use kasra, and both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: ما بال النسوة بضم النون الأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭb is a serious matter that gives occasion for addressing someone; حصحص الحق may mean truth's share and direction became distinct from falsehood.
rows.anchor: الخطب الأمر الذي يعظم شأنه فيخاطب الإنسان فيه صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects حصحص to cutting hair to the skin, so the phrase means truth was separated from falsehood through its disclosure; the source cites poetry and the camel's kneeling marks.
rows.anchor: هو مكرر من قولهم حص شعره إذا استأصل قطعه وأزاله عن الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd is a stratagem designed to bring harm to another person.
rows.anchor: والكيد الاحتيال لإيصال الضرر إلى الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك is nominative as a subject or predicate, while ما رحم ربي is accusative as an exception.
rows.anchor: ذلك مرفوع بالابتداء وإن شئت على خبر الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf refuses to leave until the king learns the women's affair and his innocence; he asks about all the women rather than naming the Aziz's wife, out of courtesy to her status or because the women were witnesses against her.
rows.anchor: حين أتاه الرسول فقال: ارجع إلى ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet says he would have required release before giving the king his interpretation.
rows.anchor: ولو كنت مكانه ما أخبرتهم حتى أشترط أن يخرجوني من السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says he would have hastened to answer the summons and leave prison.
rows.anchor: ولو كنت مكانه ولبثت في السجن ما لبث لأسرعت الإجابة وبادرتهم الباب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet praises Yusuf's patience and generosity, saying that the Prophet would have asked for release before interpreting the dream and would have left prison immediately when summoned.
rows.anchor: لقد عجبت من يوسف وكرمه وصبره والله يغفر له حين سئل عن البقرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says God knows the women's plot and can reveal his innocence; Abu Muslim instead understands 'my lord' as the Aziz, but the author prefers God.
rows.anchor: أي إن الله عالم بكيدهن قادر على إظهار براءتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asks the women what happened when they tried to seduce Yusuf; they declare God free of this and testify that they knew no evil of him.
rows.anchor: هذه كلمة تنزيه أي نزهن يوسف مما اتهم به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan's confession that truth is clear means it has become manifest and firmly established; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada are cited.
rows.anchor: ظهر وتبين وحصل على أمكن وجوهه عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz's wife admits that she seduced Yusuf and lied in accusing him; her lost hope in him led her to tell the truth, and God thereby removed any remaining doubt about his innocence.
rows.anchor: اعترفت بالكذب على نفسها فيما اتهم يوسف به وإنما حملها على الصدق انقطاع طمعها منه

rows.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك، أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Yusuf's words mean that he handled the king's messenger this way so the king or Aziz would know he had not betrayed him concerning his wife in his absence.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي فعلت من ردي رسول الملك إليه في شأن النسوة ليعلم الملك أو العزيز

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، ابن كثير
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Ibn Kathir read the opening إن with kasra; several others use an unlengthened opening أن, while Abu ʿAmr, Qalun, and Zayd lengthen it, and the remainder use two hamzas.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير إنك لأنت يوسف بكسر الهمزة وقرأ نافع ويعقوب

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to Ubayy is أنك أو أنت يوسف; Ibn Jinni explains it as a hesitation followed by the clarification أنا يوسف.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة أبي أنك أو أنت يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir alone retains the yāʾ in من يتقي in both connected and paused reading; the other readers omit it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحده من يتقي بياء في الوصل والوقف والباقون بغير ياء

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats the open-hamza reading as an interrogative, parallel to asking whether God's favor is being claimed.
rows.anchor: أنه على الاستفهام كأنه قال: أو تلك نعمة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects a poetic analogy for dropping the yāʾ and instead treats من as a relative pronoun, 'the one who fears'; the following verb can coordinate by meaning because the construction resembles a conditional.
rows.anchor: لا يحمل على نحو قول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical coordination is compared to the reading فأصدق وأكن and to a jussive reading of ويذرهم in another verse.
rows.anchor: وأكن حملت وأكن على موضع الفاء

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan heard رسلنا لديهم with a vowelless lām; this supports treating the final form as lightened in pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن أنه سمع رسلنا لديهم يكتبون بإسكان اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izjāʾ means driving or moving something little by little; it can describe scraping by on small means or accepting a meagre, deficient amount.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة: وهبت الريح من تلقاء ذي أرل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic and poetic examples use izjāʾ for moving clouds and camels, and for a poor commodity accepted only by coaxing the buyer.
rows.anchor: وفلان يزجي العيش أي يدفع بالقليل ويكتفي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann is a blessing; its root sense is cutting because a gift cuts the recipient off from poverty.
rows.anchor: والمن النعمة وأصله القطع لأنها تقطع المنعم عليه من حال بؤسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār is preferring one thing over another, related to choosing and selecting and rooted in giving priority to what leaves a good أثر.
rows.anchor: والإيثار تفضيل أحد الشيئين على الآخر ونظيره الاختيار والاجتباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭaʾ is the opposite of correctness; the source gives its forms and cites a line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: الخطأ ضد الصواب. يقال: خطأ الرجل يخطأ خطأ

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي، أبو عبيدة، ثعلب، أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Tathrīb means reproach: Ibn al-Aʿrabi gives rebuking, Abu ʿUbayda derives it from corruption, Thaʿlab says counting another's sins, and Abu Muslim connects it to inner fat for emphatic blame.
rows.anchor: التثريب التوبيخ يقال: ثرب وأثرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل علمتم is a question intended to make the brothers acknowledge the matter; ما فعلتم is an object clause, and God's promise to reward the good is the conditional response.
rows.anchor: هل علمتم استفهام والمراد به التقرير ما فعلتم بيوسف تقديره أي شيء فعلتم بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them 'the good-doers' replaces a pronoun because fearing God and being patient are themselves forms of good action.
rows.anchor: وذكر المحسنين ناب عن الضمير العائد إلى من لأن الاتقاء والصبر في معنى الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لا تثريب عليكم, تثريب is an indefinite singular noun built with لا; عليكم is not governed by it but supplies an understood predicate or description, and اليوم may attach in several ways.
rows.anchor: تثريب نكرة مفردة مبنية مع لا على الفتح ولا يجوز أن يتعلق عليكم به

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers attaching اليوم to the next clause, so the phrase means 'today God forgives you'; the same syntax applies to لا ريب فيه.
rows.anchor: وهذا اختيار الأخفش وهكذا الكلام في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers also complained that their livestock had perished and other afflictions had struck them.
rows.anchor: إنهم شكوا ما نالهم من هلاك مواشيهم والبلاء الذي أصابهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الجبائي
rows.claim: A meagre offering may be poor goods accepted only at a reduced price, according to Ibn Abbas and al-Jubbaʾi; other commentators call it merely little.
rows.anchor: رديئة لا تؤخذ إلا بوكس عن ابن عباس والجبائي

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس، ابن أبي مليكة، عبد الله بن الحارث، الكلبي، مقاتل، سعيد بن جبير، الحسن، الضحاك
rows.claim: Reported identifications of their goods include debased coins, a worn sack and rope, Bedouin wool and ghee, pine nuts and green grain, bad coins, dried curds, sandals and hides, or powdered fruit pulp.
rows.anchor: لا تنفق في ثمن الطعام عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask Yusuf to give full measure despite their poor payment and to be generous with the price; another reading of their plea asks him to return Benjamin.
rows.anchor: كما كنت توفي في السنين الماضية ولا تنظر إلى قلة بضاعتنا في هذه السنة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج، الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Dahhak take تصدق علينا as a request to give their brother back.
rows.anchor: معناه تصدق علينا برد أخينا عن ابن جريج والضحاك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu ʿAbd Allah recounts Jacob's letter to Egypt's ruler: he tells of twenty years of trials, Joseph's disappearance and Benjamin's detention, and asks for Benjamin's release, fair grain, and full measure.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب النبوة بالإسناد عن الحسن بن محبوب عن أبي إسماعيل الفراء عن طربال عن أبي عبد الله ع في خبر طويل

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Jacob's letter identifies his lineage and recalls Abraham's rescue from the fire before narrating the family's trials.
rows.anchor: يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن صاحب نمرود الذي جمع له النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن
rows.claim: The letter says the brothers claimed Benjamin stole the king's measure, though Jacob insists his household does not steal.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أنه سرق مكيال الملك ونحن أهل بيت لا نسرق وقد حبسته عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers recognized Yusuf when his smile showed teeth like pearls, according to Ibn Abbas; another account says he removed his crown.
rows.anchor: فلما أبصروا ثناياه وكانت كاللؤلؤ المنظوم شبهوه بيوسف

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Yusuf's use of his own name rather than 'I am he' emphasizes that he is the brother whom they wronged and nearly killed.
rows.anchor: أظهر الاسم ولم يقل أنا هو تعظيما لما وقع به من ظلم إخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf calls Benjamin his brother as another wronged person like himself, and says God reunited them after a long separation.
rows.anchor: لأن قصدوه وهذا المظلوم كظلمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever fears God and is patient through hardship and away from sin will receive the full reward of the good-doers.
rows.anchor: على المصائب وعن المعاصي { فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers admit they sinned and say God favored Yusuf with patience, knowledge, reason, beauty, and kingship; their admission shows remorse rather than persistence.
rows.anchor: فضلك واختارك الله علينا بالحلم والعلم والعقل والحسن والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf promises no blame or reproach today and asks God to forgive their past sin, saying he will seek forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: لا تعيير ولا توبيخ ولا تقريع عليكم الآن فيما فعلتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣl means separation or cutting; a judge is called faṣīl because he settles and cuts through disputes.
rows.anchor: الفصل أصله القطع ومنه قيل للحاكم فيصل لأنه يقطع الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafnīd means weakening someone's judgment; another derivation calls it corruption, supported by poetry.
rows.anchor:
والتفنيد تضعيف لرأي قال:
يا صاحبي دعا لومي وتفنيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the caravan left Egypt and headed toward Syria, Jacob told his descendants with him that he could smell Yusuf.
rows.anchor: لما خرجت القافلة وانفصلت من مصر متوجهة نحو الشام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allah reports that Jacob smelled Yusuf's shirt as the caravan departed from ten days' distance in Palestine; other estimates are eight nights, eighty farsakhs, or a month's journey.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: وجد يعقوب ريح قميص يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a wind carried the scent of Yusuf's shirt to Jacob; a story says the east wind sought and received permission to bring it before the bearer arrived.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هاجت ريح فحملت بريح قميص يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Lāwlā an tufannidūn means 'if only you would not call me foolish,' according to Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
rows.anchor: لولا أن تسفهوني عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets it as 'if only you would not weaken my judgment.'
rows.anchor: لولا أن تضعفوني في الرأي عن ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، السدي، الضحاك، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Other explanations are 'call me a liar' or 'say I am old, senile, and have lost my mind'; Ibn Abbas is also reported with the liar interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير والسدي والضحاك. وروي ذلك أيضا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob means that he is certain the scent is Yusuf's; the other readings describe what he fears his sons will say.
rows.anchor: وتقديره إني أقطع أنها ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

rows.speaker: قتادة، الحسن
rows.claim: The brothers say Jacob remains in his old error of loving Yusuf and hoping he will return, not religious misguidance; they believe Yusuf died long ago.
rows.anchor: وإنما أرادوا به المبالغة في حب يوسف والأماني الفاسدة فيما كان يرجو من عوده بعد موته عن قتادة والحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Another interpretation of their words is that Jacob remains in his old grief.
rows.anchor: معناه إنك لفي شقائك القديم عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase shows that قديم can mean something earlier or longstanding in ordinary language.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن لفظ القديم قد يطلق في اللغة على المتقدم في الوجود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The bearer of good news was Judah according to one report from Ibn Abbas, and Malik ibn Dhiʿr in another.
rows.anchor: وهو يهوذا عن ابن عباس وفي رواية أخرى عنه أنه مالك بن ذعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer cast Yusuf's shirt onto Jacob's face, restoring his sight; al-Dahhak adds that his strength, youth, and joy also returned.
rows.anchor: ألقى البشير قميص يوسف على وجه يعقوب فعاد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob told the bearer that he did not know how to repay him except by asking God to ease his death agonies.
rows.anchor: ما أدري ما أثيبك به هون الله عليك سكرات الموت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Jacob says he knew God would fulfil Yusuf's dream and relieve His prophets through patience; al-Hasan says God had told Jacob Yusuf was alive but not where he was.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كان الله سبحانه أعلمه بحياته ولم يعلمه بمكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase لا يكاد يسيغه describes something not readily swallowed; in لم يكد يراها, the intended meaning is that the person did not see it.
rows.anchor:
وما لم يقع مثل قوله:
لم يكد يراها
[النور: 40] لأن المعنى لم يرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثل الذين كفروا is estimated as 'the likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord' or treated as an inserted word; their deeds are a genitive-like appositional subject and 'ashes' is the predicate.
rows.anchor: مثل الذين كفروا تقديره فيما يتلى عليكم مثل الذين كفروا بربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers threatened to expel the messengers unless they returned to the disbelievers' religion and doctrines.
rows.anchor: أي من بلادنا { أو لتعودن في ملتنا } أي إلا أن ترجعوا إلى أدياننا ومذاهبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised the messengers that He would destroy their unjust opponents and give the messengers their land afterward, telling them to endure until that promise was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: أهلك عدوكم وأورثكم أرضهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever harms his neighbor will inherit the neighbor's house.
rows.anchor: من آذى جاره ورثه الله داره
